profiles.output: Generic ffmpeg CLI with GPL/libx264 features
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Exact features vary with native configure options and platform libraries.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Upstream ffmpeg CLI with browser-target constraints; arbitrary CLI arguments are supported.

comparison.name: ffmpeg.wasm core
comparison.note: Reference comparison only; not maintained by WASM Zoo.

notes: Full means a broad software FFmpeg build for the browser target, not every capability of every native FFmpeg build.
Both full profiles require SharedArrayBuffer and COOP/COEP because the upstream FFmpeg CLI requires a working thread backend.
Native networking, libavdevice capture APIs and hardware acceleration backends are deliberately reported as unsupported rather than hidden.
Each built release records actual file sizes, SHA-256 hashes, enabled FFmpeg CONFIG entries, features.json and ffmpeg-config.mak.

packages.name: ImageMagick
packages.summary: Upstream magick CLI compiled for browser WebAssembly with reproducible source and toolchain pins.

profiles.label: Browser Full
profiles.output: Generic upstream magick CLI; input and output paths are chosen by CLI arguments
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Feature set depends on optional delegate libraries and platform integration available in the native build.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Upstream magick CLI with browser filesystem constraints and PNG/JPEG-focused delegate set.

notes: The browser-full profile is deliberately single-threaded: ImageMagick thread support and OpenMP are disabled, the CLI runs inside an outer Worker, and SharedArrayBuffer/cross-origin isolation are not required.
Files live in Emscripten MEMFS during each command; native filesystem watches, device access, fonts and shell pipes are not equivalent to a desktop build.
ImageMagick zero-configuration mode is enabled so the browser build does not depend on external delegates.xml/config files.
v0.4.0 enables zlib, PNG and JPEG support. Optional delegates such as TIFF, WebP, HEIC, OpenEXR, LCMS, XML, Ghostscript/PDF and font stacks remain disabled and are recorded as capability gaps.
The real Chromium smoke test runs magick -version, identifies a PNG fixture, resizes it and writes a JPEG output.
Pages stages the published release core and uses the current runtime wrapper for the Playground, matching the FFmpeg/libarchive pattern.

ImageMagick 7.1.2 detects PNG through pkg-config; Emscripten 6.0.6 provides libpng 1.6.58 without libpng.pc, so the builder supplies a target-only pkg-config shim that points back to the pinned Emscripten port.

The browser-full builder applies a narrowly scoped source patch for zero-configuration mode: the one-time anonymous pixel-cache mmap decision is initialized to disabled. With an empty built-in policy and no working Emscripten mmap this preserves the effective behavior while avoiding ImageMagick's policy/semaphore initialization cycle during first pixel-cache open.

profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Feature set depends on optional compression, crypto, XML and platform libraries available at native build time.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Upstream bsdtar/bsdcpio/bsdcat/bsdunzip CLIs with browser filesystem constraints and zlib+bzip2 enabled.

notes: The browser profile is single-threaded and does not require SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation.
Files live in Emscripten MEMFS during each command; native filesystem metadata and process semantics are not equivalent to a desktop build.
v0.3.0 intentionally leaves xz/LZMA, Zstandard, LZ4, LZO, XML and crypto backends disabled and records those gaps explicitly.
The real Chromium smoke test lists and extracts a ZIP/Deflate fixture and also instantiates the other published CLI cores.
Emscripten 6.0.6 pins zlib 1.3.2 and bzip2 1.0.6 for the enabled ports; their license notices ship with the binary release.
